title: The need for standardized tracking of investments in digital health
authors: Mathieson, KM; Forslund, M
abstract:
This article examines the need for standardized tracking of investments in digital health to improve transparency, coordination and accountability in support of universal health coverage. It analyses current challenges in the digital health financing landscape, including fragmented funding streams, inconsistent investment classifications, limited reporting mechanisms and the absence of a globally agreed taxonomy for digital health investments. Drawing on lessons from financing frameworks used in other areas of global health, the article argues that improved visibility of funding flows would strengthen strategic planning, identify investment gaps, support alignment with national priorities and enable more effective coordination among governments, development partners and private sector stakeholders.

The publication proposes the development of a global digital health investment taxonomy to provide a standardized framework for classifying and reporting investments across stakeholders. It discusses recommendations for the taxonomy’s design, adoption and integration into existing national and international reporting systems, including health accounts and development assistance mechanisms. The authors conclude that systematic tracking of digital health investments would support evidence-based decision-making, improve accountability and resource allocation, strengthen health systems and primary health care, and contribute to more equitable and sustainable progress towards universal health coverage.

title: Microplanning for primary health care:  implementation guide for reaching the unreached: web annex A: workshop to support the introduction and use of the WHO microplanning for primary health care guide: facilitators’ slides
authors: World Health Organization
abstract:
This facilitators’ slide deck supports workshops introducing and applying the WHO guide Microplanning for primary health care: implementation guide for reaching the unreached. It provides a structured framework for understanding and practicing microplanning as a collaborative process involving health services, communities and other stakeholders to improve equitable access to integrated health interventions. The material explains key concepts, including unreached populations, unmet need, effective coverage, equity analysis and stakeholder engagement, and situates microplanning within existing district and facility planning and review cycles.

The workshop content follows the main stages of the microplanning process: diagnosis of service gaps and unreached populations, analysis of barriers and root causes, development and prioritization of solutions, implementation planning, and monitoring, learning and review. Through plenary sessions, group exercises, spreadsheet tools and practical templates, participants are guided in analysing performance against targets, identifying demand- and supply-side barriers, prioritizing actions, developing facility and health worker microplans, and establishing mechanisms for monitoring progress. The slides also support planning for capacity-building needs and integration of microplanning into routine health system management processes.

title: Blueprint for strengthening responses to fungal diseases and antifungal resistance: implementation guidance
authors: World Health Organization
abstract:
This implementation guidance provides a practical framework to strengthen national and regional responses to fungal disease and antifungal resistance by translating the WHO fungal priority pathogens list into feasible, context-adaptable actions. Developed in response to requests from Member States and partners, it addresses persistent gaps in awareness, diagnostics, surveillance, treatment, workforce capacity and health system preparedness that limit effective prevention and management of fungal diseases. Aligned with the Global action plan on antimicrobial resistance, universal health coverage and One Health principles, the guidance supports countries in integrating fungal disease into existing public health programmes and coordinated national strategies.

The publication organizes priority actions within four interconnected domains: public health and health system interventions; therapies, technologies and innovation systems; laboratory systems, surveillance and outbreak preparedness; and social, environmental and One Health drivers. It outlines implementation approaches, monitoring and priority-setting processes to support phased adaptation according to national capacities and contexts. Developed through expert consultation, evidence synthesis and consensus-based prioritization, the guidance aims to strengthen governance, improve equitable access to diagnostics and antifungal medicines, enhance surveillance and stewardship, foster research and innovation, and promote coordinated, sustainable action to reduce the burden of fungal disease and mitigate antifungal resistance.
